signals.title: NZD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + BoJ Hike Speculation
signals.text: The G10 scorecard indicates JPY outperforming peers with a 1W average of +1.396% across 7 pairs, while NZD lags at -0.736% across 4 pairs, creating a 2.132% leader-to-laggard divergence. The move accelerates as markets ramp up bets on an upcoming BoJ rate hike, pushing spot downward against a +335bp nominal policy rate spread that structurally favors NZD via RBNZ 2.75% vs BoJ 1.0%. JPY leveraged funds net short sits crowded at -111,297 contracts (2nd percentile of its 52-week range), driving an aggressive short-covering squeeze across yen crosses. Meanwhile, NZD data momentum remains stagnant with ESI at -1.7 against JPY's +28.7 beat rate. The BEER valuation model registers an extreme stretch on NZD/JPY at z = -3.29σ below model fair value. Trade bias: Bearish NZD/JPY, driven by JPY short squeeze and cross-scorecard divergence. Catalyst: BoJ meeting 18 Sep. Risk: BoJ holds rates at 1.0% without hawkish guidance, prompting carry reinstatement.

signals.title: USD/CAD — Geopolitical Supply Shock vs Carry
signals.text: USD/CAD trades at 1.3776, holding below its SMA20 at 1.3848, SMA50 at 1.3988, and SMA200 at 1.3831. Crude supply disruption headlines following Iranian naval attacks on ten vessels in the Strait of Hormuz push WTI higher to $94.30/bbl, providing clear terms-of-trade support for the Canadian Dollar. However, Fed at 3.75% vs BoC at 2.25% generates a +150bp policy spread and a +136bp SOFR-CORRA carry advantage that structurally cushions the US Dollar. Leveraged funds hold CAD net short at -70,142 contracts (10th percentile of its 52-week range), leaving the pair vulnerable to continued short covering if energy markets price an extended transit closure. Trade bias: Bearish USD/CAD; sustained energy disruption pressures technical moving average cluster. Catalyst: BoC meeting 9 Sep. Risk: Hormuz maritime traffic normalizes rapidly, removing CAD commodity support and restoring USD carry dominance.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Downside Skew + Positioning Unwind
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 153.50, breaking below its technical cluster of SMA20 at 158.45, SMA50 at 160.16, and SMA200 at 158.43. Saxo 25-delta risk reversals trade at an extreme put skew of -2.46 for 1M tenor, showing heavy institutional demand for base-currency downside protection. Leveraged funds JPY net short expanded by -29,678 WoW to -111,297 contracts (2nd percentile, z = -2.18σ), setting up acute squeeze dynamics despite Fed 3.75% vs BoJ 1.0% offering a +267bp SOFR-TONA carry buffer. Volatility risk premium sits negative at -0.7% (IV 10.6% vs HV30 11.3%), reflecting thin options supply relative to realized swings. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY; options downside skew and speculative squeeze overpower carry. Catalyst: BoJ meeting 18 Sep. Risk: Resumption of US Treasury yield rally widens the 2-year yield gap and arrests yen buying.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Positioning + Vol + Retail Extreme
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7226, holding comfortably above its SMA20 at 0.7151, SMA50 at 0.7054, and SMA200 at 0.6995. CFTC positioning shows institutional leveraged funds crowded long at +50,250 contracts (94th percentile, z = +1.79σ), yet WoW net flows fell by -3,328 contracts to signal late-trend deceleration. In contrast, retail sentiment sits at an extreme 91% short, establishing an institutional-versus-retail divergence that risks an aggressive squeeze if resistance clears. Saxo 1M ATM IV at 7.2% vs HV30 at 5.9% yields a +1.2% vol risk premium, indicating the options market is paying up for trend protection rather than chasing delta outright. RBA at 4.35% vs Fed at 3.75% provides a -60bp carry advantage to AUD that keeps dips supported. Trade bias: Long AUD/USD; retail short capitulation supports bullish continuation. Catalyst: US PPI release 9 Sep. Risk: Commodity prices reverse sharply, triggering an institutional crowded-long liquidation.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Technical Resistance Ahead of ECB
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1635, directly testing its descending SMA200 at 1.1638 while holding above the SMA20 at 1.1619 and SMA50 at 1.1520. Fed policy at 3.75% vs ECB at 2.4% maintains a +135bp nominal policy spread and a +146bp SOFR-€STR carry premium favoring USD, keeping broader upside structurally contained. Speculative positioning remains moderately short with leveraged funds at -52,784 contracts (31st percentile), showing limited institutional appetite to bid the pair aggressively ahead of the upcoming European Central Bank rate decision. With options 25d risk reversal balanced at -0.21 and implied volatility contained at 5.1% (VRP +0.5%), markets are pricing limited directional breakout premium prior to official policy confirmation. Trade bias: Neutral EUR/USD; upside constrained by carry deficit and technical moving-average resistance. Catalyst: ECB Monetary Policy Statement 10 Sep. Risk: ECB delivers an unexpectedly hawkish policy guidance stance, forcing an immediate close above 1.1640.
